p15_140ContourArtMeshYaw.next: Acquire drawn hair-strand identity and closed boundary masks across keyviews, with independent face/neck/coat underpaint; test mesh with actual occlusion correspondence before selecting full yaw.

p15_141SourceStrandCorrespondenceGate.visualFindings: Source-keyframe hair masks are not physically corresponding ArtMesh textures. Forward/reverse texture projection mismatches cluster at 112.5-to-135 rear hair and face/ear, and at 90-to-112.5 crown/ahoge. The appearance-based hair masks also contain face/eye ink, invalidating blind shared-mesh texture deformation.
p15_141SourceStrandCorrespondenceGate.next: Correct the actual source RGBA layers by strand identity and separate face/ear material from hair. Approve physical anchors and matching underpaint across keyviews before source-key VDD rerender.

p15_142FaceHairOwnership.visualFindings: Image-space protection of eye/ear/nose/chin pixels removes part of the incorrect hair deformation. The best tested radius slightly reduces adjacent-frame error, but face ink fragments at 101.25° and irregular hair fringe / ahoge at 123.75° remain visibly unacceptable.
p15_142FaceHairOwnership.next: Obtain verified, separable source-painted eye/ear/front hair and rear hair RGBA parts, register actual hair-root/tip tracks and hidden material across 90/112.5/135; rerender without stretching face ink.

p15_143IndependentFrontBangs.visualFindings: Independent transparent front fringe part has source-like line and pink color palette, but full-overlay review covers the visible near eye and duplicates frontal bangs. Placement and strand identity are not registered to the canonical 112.5° painting.
p15_143IndependentFrontBangs.next: Align new front-bangs painted part with source hair ownership and remove source-overlapping bangs before compositing; confirm face and eye underpaint, then test actual ArtMesh displacement and 90–135 yaw.

p15_144BangsAlignmentAndYaw.visualFindings: Affine registration reduces front bangs misplacement and maintains eye ownership but the independently generated strand material duplicates existing hairlines and produces cheek/neck gaps. At 101.25° and 123.75°, DIS interpolation still ghosts the ahoge and hair texture; new midview key increases max frame discontinuity.
p15_144BangsAlignmentAndYaw.next: Redraw front-bangs source aligned to canonical 112.5° hair-root/eye geometry and replace matching source hair pixels with a coherent underpaint, then validate semantic strand identities before ArtMesh yaw interpolation.

p15_145CanonicalFringeSourceTransfer.textureReference: P15-143 native independent bangs painting registered in P15-144
p15_145CanonicalFringeSourceTransfer.pixelIntegrity: Canonical alpha, eye, face and non-fringe pixels maintained; original files unchanged
p15_145CanonicalFringeSourceTransfer.visualFindings: Source-owned fringe silhouette avoids duplicated overlaid bangs, keeps eye facial ink and modestly reduces five-angle frame RGB variation. Source hair/ahoge still ghosts at 101.25/123.75 and jacket/collar source art differs across views; texture transfer is research-only.
p15_145CanonicalFringeSourceTransfer.next: Produce source-painted strand labels and structurally matching scalp/face/collar layers across 90/112.5/135, then test actual independent ArtMesh motion on aligned geometry.

candidateGate.reason: Source region labels have no verified material identity, and middle-angle renderings show line tears and owner switching.

p15_146SourceStrandRegionIdentity.visualFindings: Part region IDs are stable for mask storage, but physical strands are not corresponded between independently painted keys. Mesh deformation at 101.25/123.75 yields visible horizontal seams, face ink tearing, and abrupt ownership changes. Preserve P15-145 reference as current research baseline.
p15_146SourceStrandRegionIdentity.next: Generate and visually register reference-painted per-strand overlays with annotated root/tip and hidden face/neck material for each actual source key; rerender only when semantic identity is validated.

motionCandidateGate.visualFindings: The loop is truncated near its root by alpha-domain extraction; intermediate frames show dangling arcs and extra fragments.

p15_147AhogeRootTipMotion.visualFindings: Explicit two-point ahoge alignment can transform the native loop geometrically, but cropped visible art has an incomplete root. Intermediate frames create dangling and duplicated loops; continuity worsens compared with source-owned P15-145.
p15_147AhogeRootTipMotion.next: Obtain a complete authored looped-ahoge isolated RGBA part and its root attachment/hidden scalp source at all three keyviews. Validate exact source registration before shared deform.

p15_148NativeAhogeRegistration.visualFindings: One original isolated RGBA loop ahoge has been painted and checked. Bounded registration moves it toward the canonical 112.5-degree root. Single-owner upper-loop replacement reduces duplicate-overlap artifact but a visible crossing and clipped right loop leg remain at the crown; 90-135 continuity is worse than original source baseline.
p15_148NativeAhogeRegistration.next: Paint an aligned complete ahoge loop at each source key including both crown attachment roots and underlying scalp material. Use source-owner replacement with full root identity before continuous yaw ArtMesh.

p15_149AhogeCrownAttachment.visualFindings: Opacity tapering reconnects the independent loop to the existing 112.5-degree hair crown more smoothly than a hard horizontal cut, but the loop tail remains clipped and root linework still diverges. The source canonical arc is visually preferable and continues to be used as baseline.
p15_149AhogeCrownAttachment.next: Obtain exact aligned 90/112.5/135 part artwork including both attached roots and hidden crown scalp. Only retest when a visually coherent source can replace the failed root seam.

visualFindings.yaw090: Generated loop is a disconnected arch with incomplete double-root attachment, and registered replacement shows a thin duplicate root stroke.
visualFindings.yaw112p5: Source-aligned part retains a root crossing and loop tail mismatch.
visualFindings.yaw135: Generated loop and root placement differ from source; registered replacement still leaves overlapping hair arcs.
visualFindings.intermediates: At 101.25 and 123.75 degrees, double loops and source face/garment ghosting remain visible.

p15_150ThreeViewIndependentAhoge.next: Correct both roots and loop shape per source view and paint source-matched hidden crown. Verify zero overlapping loop strokes and continuity at intermediate yaw before ArtMesh admission.

p15_151DoubleRootAttachment.visualFindings: 90-degree generated loop has two free roots terminating around y55 without penetrating crown. Piecewise geometric lengthening to y81 reaches y75 and slightly decreases the maximum five-frame pixel difference, but does not resolve double ink strokes or source-matched hidden crown anatomy.
p15_151DoubleRootAttachment.next: Source-paint both 90-degree roots under the correct hair crown. Check 112.5/135 root contours and hidden scalp, then perform whole-head motion and occlusion validation.

p15_152NativeRootPatchQA.visualFindings: Native generated root patch contains broad near-transparent grey-white haze beyond target crown. Cropping it to a bounded alpha domain prevents global background pollution and gives a slight motion metric improvement, but extra ink and misregistered root connection remain visible. Source-painted physical scalp continuity is not established.
p15_152NativeRootPatchQA.next: Generate or paint source-matched ahoge double-root attachment and scalp underpaint with strict alpha and exact geometry; require close-up keyview quality before whole-head yaw tests.

p15_153CanonicalAhogeSourceTopology.visualFindings: The original profile displays a broad loop and fine adjacent stroke; their visible alpha merges into one connected component at all three tested viewpoints. Source reconstruction is lossless, but connected-component partitioning does not distinguish their physical roots. A generated short-root patch depicts different anatomy.
p15_153CanonicalAhogeSourceTopology.next: Author matched loop and thin-strand roots from original source geometry, separating the joined alpha strokes by semantic drawing; paint hidden attachment before evaluating cross-view motion.

p15_154VisibleSourceStrandParts.visualFindings: The main loop and manually bounded left stroke can be stored in source-exact transparent layers, but isolated stroke translation reveals holes and disconnects part of the visible loop. The cut is a source-pixel partition, not a verified second physically independent strand.
p15_154VisibleSourceStrandParts.next: Artist-align a continuous second strand root/edge mask from canonical 90° source and paint corresponding hidden crown pixels. Require clean 2/4/8px independent motion before mapping to other yaw keys.

p15_155AnchoredCrownVisibleLoop.geometryFindings: Tapered vertex displacement holds canonical pixels at and below y54 and eliminates new opaque-crown alpha holes for 2,4,8px displacement. Transparency exposed above the hairline is air and is correctly left transparent.
p15_155AnchoredCrownVisibleLoop.visualFindings: At 8px the visible left loop boundary still produces a doubled line; the 55-pixel partition represents a segment of the major loop contour, not an artist-verified distinct hair strand.
p15_155AnchoredCrownVisibleLoop.next: Treat the left line as part of the full loop, build a single continuous loop boundary and a root-fixed deformation over that complete part; check 8px close-up before three-keyview transfer.

p15_156WholeLoopArtMesh.motionGeometry: source-owned connected silhouette; pixel-sampled smooth inverse warp with root fixed
p15_156WholeLoopArtMesh.visualFindings: The complete visible source loop bends as one shape under a smooth root-fixed warp. Enlarged 8px frames show a continuous curve and attached crown without doubled left-leg line. Source crown below y54 is unchanged.
p15_156WholeLoopArtMesh.next: Apply the same source-owned continuous-loop segmentation to 112.5/135 views, then validate matching visible loop attachment and five-angle interpolation against baseline.

p15_157ThreeViewWholeLoopVDD.visualFindings: Separate whole-loop flow and anchored source-owner warp produce disconnected intermediate loop segments at 101.25 and 123.75 degrees. Native key art remains exact but the source hair root and crown material are not anatomically corresponded.
p15_157ThreeViewWholeLoopVDD.next: Register the same loop root and tip across all three source views with a painted hidden crown, then validate intermediate frame topology.

p15_158AnchorAlignedLoopCorrespondence.visualFindings: Root/apex similarity alignment permits preserving individual source loop silhouettes but signed-distance mask fusion collapses the 101.25-degree arc to a small fragment; nearest-owner source art keeps the 101.25 loop but leaves disconnected crown strokes and a broken root at 123.75 degrees.

acceptanceGate.reason: Both signed-distance fusion and nearest-owner transforms have disconnected or unregistered root segments. Two point anchors do not establish corresponding loop boundaries.

p15_158AnchorAlignedLoopCorrespondence.next: Establish full-loop source control points and painter-verified root/crown underpaint per view; replace endpoint-only correspondence with curve-aware matching and verify single-loop root continuity at both mid angles.

p15_159FiveControlLoopCorrespondence.visualFindings: Five view-space controls retain a substantially fuller intermediate loop than distance-field mask blending, but 101.25 and 123.75 degree renders retain root strokes, separated upper-hair components and misregistered crown boundaries. A local synthetic root bridge produces an extra intersection stroke. Do not select either candidate as the canonical VDD renderer.

acceptanceGate.reason: Source root pixels cross the experimental upper-hair boundary; 101.25 and 123.75 show extra connected components, remaining crown strokes and owner-switch discontinuity.

p15_159FiveControlLoopCorrespondence.next: Create source-registered inner/outer strand edges and matching root attachment/hidden scalp, then test intermediate curve connectivity and all native keyframes before updating VDD.

p15_160RootOwnershipUnderpaint.findings: All three original source root landmarks are below the y54 visible-loop extraction cut, leaving zero material pixels beneath the cut. Synthetic bounded inpainting cannot restore actual root attachment, and the 101.25/123.75 intermediate crowns remain disconnected. Preserve the original reference pipeline.

acceptanceGate.reason: All source root anchors fall below the extracted material boundary; synthetic underpaint neither supplies root semantics nor produces connected intermediate silhouettes.

p15_160RootOwnershipUnderpaint.next: Replace y54 proxy extraction with separate source-painted loop/roots and matched hidden crown material for each view, then rerender and require connected roots at both intermediate angles.

p15_161SourceRootExtraction.visualFindings: Direct extraction from the uncropped original key art finds no eligible root pixels at 90/135 degrees and only three at 112.5. Five-angle renders still show broken intermediate arcs and crown seams. The original source linework cannot reliably be separated into physical hair roots using local dark-pixel heuristics.

acceptanceGate.reason: No view-complete root was extracted from whole source art; at most three extra 112.5-degree pixels were found and intermediate loops remain broken. Source-derived line masks are not artist-verified root material.

p15_161SourceRootExtraction.next: Acquire source-registered painted root layers and a matching hidden crown for each keyview; rerun only when the per-view root part extends to its actual attachment with visually continuous material.

p15_162RootArtworkCandidates.visualFindings: Two newly generated transparent source-root candidates were assessed with the previously generated 135-degree root part. The 90-degree roots stop before y75, all three source-top silhouette IoU values are below 0.16, and yaw 101.25 has detached hair remnants while yaw 123.75 has an oversized loop passing through crown artwork. Root-material correspondence and underpaint are not acceptable.
p15_162RootArtworkCandidates.next: Revise the independent RGBA loop art with exact canonical reference alignment at each yaw. Require root extension, top silhouette match and human-readable local closeups to pass before any VDD updates.

p15_163CanonicalLoopRegistration.visibleFindings: Three independent loop sources now align more closely with their source-visible canonical loop silhouettes and meet the actual root-row contact proxy. Both intermediate frames still exhibit inaccurate hair ownership, with a detached ink fragment at 101.25 degrees and an unnatural root/loop overlap at 123.75 degrees. Preserve the baseline renderer.
p15_163CanonicalLoopRegistration.next: Construct actual original-view-matched scalp underpainting with loop pixels removed and one root owner per key. Validate 101.25/123.75 mask connectivity without residual old loop before VDD admission.

p15_164LoopOwnershipAndCrown.visualFindings: Visible upper-loop source pixels are reversibly owned by a separate RGBA part, and a small crown inpaint can be generated for inspection. Intermediate 101.25-degree frame retains disconnected ink and 123.75-degree source-owned frame shows a severed root; alpha in the crown region changes after composition. Existing reference remains preferable.
p15_164LoopOwnershipAndCrown.next: Acquire a fully source-matched crown background with the original root ink explicitly painted out, and a physically attached loop root layer in each canonical view. Validate root/crown pixels at the two intermediate angles before selecting VDD.

p15_165CrownInkOwnership.visualFindings: Root-ink masks and bounded inpaint allow diagnostic removal of original attachment strokes without modifying canonical keys. 101.25-degree intermediate view still contains a separate residual strand, and the repaired 123.75-degree loop has an unnatural crown junction. Candidate alpha differs from reference in the crown region and frame-to-frame continuity remains worse than baseline.
p15_165CrownInkOwnership.next: Produce rootless crown art authored against canonical source views and full continuous root layers, then verify intermediate alpha ownership and single-loop contours before switching to independent VDD.

p15_166CrownSilhouetteOwnership.visualFindings: Morphological head-core silhouette separates above-crown loop pixels while preserving existing crown RGBA underneath. The 101.25-degree loop has a detached lower end; 123.75-degree root connection remains visually unregistered. Adjusting opening radius 5/9/13 has negligible effect on output. Native keys remain pixel exact.
p15_166CrownSilhouetteOwnership.next: Prepare matched source-painted crown and complete attached-loop roots as a paired asset, then verify per-view source reconstruction and intermediate root attachment against real frames.

p15_167CanonicalLoopEndpointPairs.hiddenCrownProvenance: source RGB with bounded synthetic inpainting; source-native RGBA and owner matte are preserved separately
p15_167CanonicalLoopEndpointPairs.next: Use the root/contact and free-tip distinction to paint a source-matched hidden crown and finished loop attachment in each view. Confirm the paired artwork closeup, then repeat 101.25/123.75° continuity and occlusion checks.

p15_168RootOcclusionOwnership.visualFindings: Root-front and crown-front variants produce a single connected upper silhouette at 101.25 and 123.75 yaw. Restricting RGB underpaint to opaque crown fixes the dark synthetic halo. Close-ups still show residual scalp ink and an unregistered hair attachment. Both variants increase max adjacent RGB MAE over reference, and source-matched painter-authored underpaint remains unverified.
p15_168RootOcclusionOwnership.next: Use the verified single-source root/crown ownership and raster exact keyframes to paint clean native crown linework and attachment shading. Check 101.25/123.75 closeups and adjacent motion before VDD admission.

p15_169RootJunctionMatting.visualFindings: An opaque-crown bounded RGB matte reduces the minor dark seam in closeups, with the six-pixel treatment the best measured variant. The source interpolation still retains short old-root ink fragments near both midway views. Larger patches worsen adjacent-frame error, and the artwork lacks a painter-authored rootless crown.
p15_169RootJunctionMatting.next: Use the root-owned canonical layer to explicitly separate old hairline strokes by semantic source material; paint matching crown linework and verify the actual junction under motion before renderer admission.

p15_170SemanticRootInkOwnership.visualFindings: Source-line morphological blackhat masking in an opaque crown-only region gives modest local improvements with a 10-level contrast threshold. Midway root ink residuals remain visible in both frames and the result still exceeds baseline adjacent-frame error; these source pixels cannot be unambiguously classified as old-root artwork without painted semantic ownership.
p15_170SemanticRootInkOwnership.next: Produce a painter-confirmed rootless crown and root-connected strand for each original view, using the validated pixel-ownership mask and source contact point. Verify local composite with zero ghost ink at 101.25/123.75 before any renderer adoption.

p15_171PairedCrownLayerInterpolation.experimentalSourceLayerMode: independent DIS crown-background interpolation with source-owned ahoge root and free-tip transform
p15_171PairedCrownLayerInterpolation.visualFindings: Independent optical flow on source-owned crown underpainting and loop/attachment motion preserves exact canonical views, body pixels, and one top connected component at both intermediate angles. The synthetic crown source still contains unregistered root pigment and view-dependent texture drift; 101.25 degree strand retains ink residue and 123.75 crown texture ghosts. None of the candidate continuity metrics beats the reference.
p15_171PairedCrownLayerInterpolation.next: Paint source-registered crown underlayers that contain no inherited root ink at 90/112.5/135, confirm separate hair identity and exact keyview compositing, then re-evaluate intermediate view appearance and motion.

p15_172CrownUnderpaintSourceAssets.visualFindings: All three original keyviews retain reversible source-matched hair and crown ownership. Bounded root RGB reconstruction is restricted to small crown patches, but the 112.5-degree vertical attachment ink and edge artifacts at 90/135 persist in direct image review. Source-visible loop identity remains valid for diagnostic layering; hidden crown painting is not yet visually approved.
p15_172CrownUnderpaintSourceAssets.next: Create source-matched rootless crown paint at 90/112.5/135, explicitly including the 112.5 crown-edge post; after visual approval, retest intermediate yaw against unchanged optical-flow baseline.

p15_173RootStubSourceOwnership.visualFindings: Source-only RGB donors limit dark fill artifacts. Narrow mask leaves a 112.5 degree vertical post. Wider repair introduces loss of natural crown hair ink near 90 and 135. No visually acceptable crown part yet.
p15_173RootStubSourceOwnership.next: Obtain corrected artist-matched crown texture and alpha edge around the 112.5-degree root, preserving 90/135 head highlights. Verify source-layer reconstruction and closeup before mid-yaw VDD tests.

p15_174AIAssistedRootTexturePatch.method: Flux.2 Klein 4B visual edit as a source-color-matched 14x14 patch donor
p15_174AIAssistedRootTexturePatch.modelOutputScope: Only 14x14 patch around root is sampled; all other generated pixels discarded
p15_174AIAssistedRootTexturePatch.model: Flux.2 Klein 4B via Hugging Face Space
p15_174AIAssistedRootTexturePatch.visualFindings: The image-edit model produces a cleaner single-point ahoge attachment in the full edited crop. Only a source-color-matched 14x14 patch was transferred to the original 443x443 RGBA source, changing 169 pixels while preserving original alpha and all pixels outside the patch. The closeup comparison shows a localized texture adjustment but the remaining narrow stem/line still requires artist review; this is not accepted as a rootless crown.
p15_174AIAssistedRootTexturePatch.next: Extend the AI-guided edit only after confirming the intended strand ownership boundary; generate a separate rootless crown and ahoge loop with explicit transparent layers, then verify lossless source-key reconstruction and mid-yaw motion.

p15_175LayeredCrownAndAhogeAssets.reference: P15-167 source ownership; P15-174 AI root texture crop
p15_175LayeredCrownAndAhogeAssets.visualFindings: The three view-native 443x443 crown/ahoge transparent layer pairs have correct origin and source ownership. Root-contact owner-matte restoration is source-pixel exact (all 3 views), but native alpha-over of 112.5-degree pair differs in 155 visible pixels and extended root-band underpainting changes source-visible pixels. Rootless crown visual closeups show a residual 112.5-degree vertical post and thin contact remnants in 90/135. The layer assets are diagnostics, not production art.
p15_175LayeredCrownAndAhogeAssets.next: Complete the 112.5-degree source-matched crown linework and semitransparent root boundary. Validate standard alpha-over keyview fidelity and absence of crown stubs at 90,112.5,135 before continuing to 101.25/123.75 yaw.

layerContracts.ahoge: source-owned RGBA strand including its root attachment
layerContracts.crownMotionUnderpaint: full reconstructed head texture/alpha for deformation and exposure
layerContracts.crownStaticKeyframe: same underpaint RGB but alpha zero under the source-owned ahoge matte

p15_176AlphaSafeCrownOwnership.visualFindings: The three layer contracts are now distinct and non-overlapping in the static keyframe composite. The motion underpaint still shows small source-root remnants at 90, 112.5, and 135 degrees; the alpha-safe keyframe version has transparent holes under the ahoge that are filled by the matching strand at rest. Artist-matched crown cleanup is still required before VDD.
p15_176AlphaSafeCrownOwnership.next: Artist-match and remove the residual root remnants in motion underpaint while preserving ahoge attachment contour. Recheck three keyviews, then run 101.25/123.75 yaw.

p15_177SourceRootCrownRepaint.materialMethod: source-ahoge ownership seed, opaque-crown pixel inpainting, separate static alpha-safe and motion crown
p15_177SourceRootCrownRepaint.visualFindings: Three keyview motion underpaints were rendered with opaque-crown owner-matte inpaint and source root-air alpha cleanup. The wider paint makes the 112.5-degree vertical root less pronounced, but a visible post and irregular scalp boundary remain; 90 and 135 retain small protrusions. Source hairline identity and high-quality hidden crown material require further original-art correction.
p15_177SourceRootCrownRepaint.next: Obtain independent source-matched clean crown art, starting with 112.5-degree root-ink post. Verify the crown-only image closeup and the source ahoge reconnection before intermediate-yaw rendering.

p15_178AIRootlessCrownRepair.model: Flux.2 Klein 4B via Hugging Face Spaces
p15_178AIRootlessCrownRepair.registrationMethod: SIFT feature matching below y=40, ratio test 0.72, RANSAC homography, then 270x150 native crop registration

layerContracts.ahoge: original source-owned RGBA loop and root attachment
layerContracts.crownMotionUnderpaint: AI-registered rootless RGB patch plus root-air alpha cleanup
layerContracts.crownStaticKeyframe: motion underpaint with alpha cleared beneath ahoge owner matte and root-air cleanup

p15_178AIRootlessCrownRepair.visualFindings: Three source-registered AI crown patches remove the detached loop-root posts from the motion underpaint. Static keyframe alpha is cleared under the original ahoge owner matte and root-air fringe; standard alpha-over reconnects the original ahoge naturally. Canonical source keyframes, source ahoge RGBA, and head pixels below y=125 remain preserved. All three closeups and full-view composites passed agent visual inspection.
p15_178AIRootlessCrownRepair.next: Use the accepted three-view crown/ahoge pair as the VDD source for 101.25 and 123.75 degree intermediate-yaw rendering. Measure root seam, silhouette continuity, and temporal stability before changing the production renderer.

p15_179RootlessCrownMidYawVDD.acceptedSourceAssets: P15-178 three-view AI rootless crown/ahoge pairs
p15_179RootlessCrownMidYawVDD.method: root-local interpolated crown underpaint + source-owner two-anchor ahoge deformation
p15_179RootlessCrownMidYawVDD.temporalMetric: Selected candidate max adjacent RGB MAE is recorded against the whole-frame flow baseline; it is 1.1% higher while eliminating the visible duplicate-loop ghost in both midviews.
p15_179RootlessCrownMidYawVDD.next: Run denser 5-degree yaw samples with the selected crown/loop layers. Measure root seam drift and temporal continuity over the full 90-135 interval; keep production renderer unchanged until dense sweep passes.

p15_180DenseYawContinuitySweep.next: Improve single-strand identity through source curve point correspondence and continuous deformation across source-owner boundaries; preserve native keyviews. Verify 5-degree sequence, root/area continuity, and visual connection before production adoption.

p15_181CurveCorrespondence.method: Extract source loop upper contour as centerline, resample by normalized arc length, interpolate control points and estimated stroke width, continue endpoint tangents to rootless crown silhouette, and sample both source textures in matching curve/normal coordinates.
p15_181CurveCorrespondence.next: Improve source texture and root-contact appearance, then reduce temporal RGB MAE below the whole-frame DIS baseline. Keep source keyviews and deep head pixels exact; rerun 5-view visual review before any dense-yaw rollout.

p15_182RootFreeTipCurve.sourceTopology: Left/root endpoint joins crown; right endpoint is visible free tip
p15_182RootFreeTipCurve.visualFindings: The source-visible right endpoint is a free tip; retaining it removes the artificial vertical right-leg connection seen in P15-181. Root tangent variants now produce one continuous arc with a source-matched crown attachment. The upper strand still shows a dark uneven edge, and the frame-wise RGB MAE remains above the whole-frame reference.
p15_182RootFreeTipCurve.next: Repair source texture sampling at the curved upper boundary using valid strand pixels, then evaluate root attachment and full 13-yaw motion under a local perceptual/temporal gate. Retain the single-root/free-tip geometry and unchanged canonical keyframes.

p15_183ValidStrandTexture.selectionRule: Among candidates with at most 25 dark antialias edge pixels, minimize adjacent RGB MAE
p15_183ValidStrandTexture.visualFindings: Source-owned alpha mask provides valid painting-color donors for extrapolation. Inpaint and alpha-normalized sampling suppress the dark upper fringe, while 75-percent valid donor mix preserves more source linework and has the lowest frame RGB MAE among methods with <=25 dark edge pixels. Remaining temporal MAE exceeds the P15-182 and DIS baselines; root detail and upper-edge AA still need visual refinement.
p15_183ValidStrandTexture.next: Use alpha-aware source donor with conservative edge blending and improved root color junction, then evaluate region-weighted temporal stability in a 13-yaw sweep before renderer adoption.

p15_184AlphaAwareTemporalSweep.selectionRule: Minimize total dark antialias edge pixels; use local ROI RGB MAE as tie-breaker. The 5-view <=25-pixel threshold is not reused because this sweep has twice as many generated intermediate views.
p15_184AlphaAwareTemporalSweep.visualFindings: 13-yaw sweep confirms a single root-connected/free-tip strand at every generated intermediate yaw and preserves the three canonical source keyframes. Higher valid-source donor proportion reduces dark edge pixels (319 at 65% to 99 at 80%) but increases local and global frame-to-frame RGB MAE. The 80% diagnostic candidate has local ROI max MAE 9.025 versus DIS baseline 7.9475, and global max MAE 7.1183 versus DIS 6.6299. The middle source keyframe at 112.5 degrees remains a visibly different loop shape from adjacent generated frames, indicating a geometric correspondence discontinuity that texture blending cannot solve.
p15_184AlphaAwareTemporalSweep.next: Resolve curve-shape correspondence across the 112.5-degree native keyframe before further texture tuning. The current interpolation creates a geometry mismatch at the middle view; evaluate source curve landmarks, tangent orientation, and width profile, retaining native keyframe pixels exactly.

p15_185KeyviewGeometryCorrespondence.method: Fritsch-Butland PCHIP 3-keyview per-coordinate Hermite with source curve control points
p15_185KeyviewGeometryCorrespondence.geometryFinding: Source-point PCHIP reduces the middle-key control derivative discontinuity, but increases the maximum adjacent curve displacement and rendered local/global RGB MAE. The 112.5-degree native loop silhouette differs visibly from the open free-tip shapes in adjacent interpolations. Three image-space keys alone do not establish a physically consistent control-point identity or width profile.
p15_185KeyviewGeometryCorrespondence.next: Establish reliable source-local 112.5-degree strand correspondence and classify the source free-tip/crown-contact topology before further interpolation. Verify source landmark and variable width profile against actual alpha silhouettes; use only measured correction to re-run 13-yaw continuity.

p15_186SourceLandmarkAudit.criticalFinding: P15-181 source_curve() samples the contour returned by P15-153 extract(), whose loop_visible mask is clipped at y=54. The resulting 160 samples lie on the full source mask boundary (mean distance-transform radius 1 px), not on its medial centerline. It must not be treated as a centerline.
p15_186SourceLandmarkAudit.next: Replace the cropped-boundary proxy with the full source-owned strand silhouette skeleton as the geometric centerline candidate. Validate endpoint identity, ordered path, per-point width profile and source pixel reconstruction; only then test endpoint-aligned centerline interpolation on 13 yaw samples. Do not reuse the P15-181 160-point contour as centerline.

p15_187FullSkeletonVDD.method: Ordered full-source skeleton root-to-tip, distance-transform width profile, per-node normal texture sampling, linear/PCHIP shape interpolation
p15_187FullSkeletonVDD.visualFindings: The full-source medial skeleton and variable stroke-width profile produce one stable curved strand through all 13 yaw positions. Linear source centerline interpolation has a smaller maximum local head-ROI RGB MAE than whole-frame DIS (7.9214 vs 7.9475), but global temporal MAE is higher (6.9209 vs 6.6299). Magnified inspection still shows slight root stretching and texture transitions, especially around the native middle source key.
p15_187FullSkeletonVDD.next: Measure root-seam and tip drift across the 13-yaw sequence, verify medial-path orientation against source masks, and refine only the observed root transition while retaining source keys and the linear variable-width centerline. Evaluate whether global temporal stability can match DIS before production integration.

p15_188RootOcclusionSweep.finding: The P15-187 strand centerline root endpoint is inside the head silhouette. The correct depth order is strand behind crown, not strand over crown. Crown-front compositing covers at least 90% of sampled centerline points that lie beneath the crown edge, hiding the root under existing source-owned scalp pixels. The root-slot variant worsens local temporal error and is not selected.
